bun-cha-ca-quy-nhon.name: Quy Nhon Fish Cake Noodle Soup
aliases: Binh Dinh Fish Cake Noodle Soup
Quy Nhon Style Fish Cake Noodles
bun-cha-ca-quy-nhon.serving_basis: Four bowls of noodle soup for a family meal.
bun-cha-ca-quy-nhon.description: Fresh rice vermicelli is served with a light fish broth and both tender steamed and fragrant fried fish cakes. Fresh vegetables are served on the side.
bun-cha-ca-quy-nhon.finished_dish: A clear, gently sweet broth with springy fish cake, intact tomato wedges and vermicelli that is not overcooked.
bun-cha-ca-quy-nhon.serving: Divide noodles and fish cake between bowls, ladle over hot broth, add scallions and herbs, and serve with greens, lime and chili.
tips: Keep the fish and pork paste cold before pounding for a springier texture.
Simmer fish bones gently and skim the surface for a clear broth.
Add fresh greens at the table so they stay crisp.

bun-cha-ca-quy-nhon.time_note: About 90 minutes, including 10 minutes to chill the fish cake mixture.

preparation_steps: Rinse the fish bones, blanch briefly and rinse again. Pat the fillet dry, then grind or pound with pork paste, some fish sauce, salt and pepper until cohesive.
Cover and chill the fish mixture for about 10 minutes. Rinse the vegetables, cut the tomatoes into wedges and slice the scallions and dill.
cooking_steps: Simmer the fish bones with onion and shallot over low heat for about 35 minutes. Skim the surface, strain out the bones, then season the broth.
Divide the fish mixture in half. Flatten and pan-fry one half until golden; spread the other half in a heatproof dish and steam for 12–15 minutes. Cool slightly and slice.
Saute garlic, gently cook the tomatoes, then add them to the broth. Simmer for about 5 minutes, add annatto oil and adjust the seasoning.
Blanch the noodles and divide among bowls. Top with both kinds of fish cake, ladle over hot broth and finish with scallions and dill. Serve with vegetables, lime and chili.

chao-ca-loc-rau-dang.name: Mekong Snakehead Fish Porridge with Bitter Herb
aliases: Mekong Snakehead Fish and Bitter Herb Congee
Snakehead Fish Porridge with Bitter Greens
chao-ca-loc-rau-dang.serving_basis: One pot of hot porridge for four people.
chao-ca-loc-rau-dang.description: Toasted rice simmers with snakehead fish and straw mushrooms, served with bitter greens, a leafy green with a gently bitter finish. Add the greens to each bowl or briefly dip them into the hot porridge.
chao-ca-loc-rau-dang.finished_dish: Soft rice grains in a savory fish broth, boneless snakehead pieces, fragrant straw mushrooms and fresh bitter greens.
chao-ca-loc-rau-dang.serving: Ladle the porridge with fish and mushrooms, top with scallions and cilantro, and serve bean sprouts and bitter greens separately.
tips: Toast the rice until fragrant but not deeply browned.
Cook the fish just until done, then remove all bones before returning it to the pot.
Briefly dip the bitter greens or add them to each bowl at serving time.

chao-ca-loc-rau-dang.time_note: About 70 minutes; the rice simmering time depends on the preferred consistency.

preparation_steps: Rinse the rice briefly and drain. Clean the snakehead fish and score its skin; rinse the bitter greens, bean sprouts and straw mushrooms.
Chop the shallots, scallions and cilantro. Set aside the bitter greens and bean sprouts for serving.
cooking_steps: Toast the rice in a dry pan until lightly golden and fragrant. Simmer the fish in about 1 liter of water until just cooked, then remove it and pick out the bones; reserve the cooking liquid.
Add the toasted rice and remaining water to the fish broth. Simmer for 30–35 minutes, stirring the bottom from time to time.
Saute the shallots, add the straw mushrooms and cook for 2–3 minutes. Add them to the porridge. Flake the boneless fish, season lightly and return it to the pot.
Simmer for another 3–5 minutes and adjust the seasoning. Serve topped with scallions and cilantro, with bitter greens and bean sprouts on the side.

ca-nuc-kho-thom.name: Braised Scad with Pineapple
ca-nuc-kho-thom.serving_basis: One pot of braised fish for four people with rice.
ca-nuc-kho-thom.description: Firm scad is gently braised with ripe pineapple for a mild sweet-and-sour balance. The glossy sauce is especially good spooned over hot rice.
ca-nuc-kho-thom.finished_dish: The fish pieces remain intact and well-seasoned, the pineapple is tender but not mushy, and the sauce has a light caramel color.
ca-nuc-kho-thom.serving: Serve hot from a small pot or transfer to a plate. Spoon over a little sauce and pair with steamed rice and boiled vegetables.
tips: Choose firm fish and pat it dry before marinating.
Cut the pineapple into moderately thick slices so it holds its shape.
Once simmering, keep the heat low and avoid stirring the fish.

ca-nuc-kho-thom.time_note: About 90 minutes, including 20 minutes to marinate the fish.

preparation_steps: Clean the fish, drain and score each piece lightly. Marinate with half the shallot, garlic, ginger, fish sauce, sugar, salt and pepper for 20 minutes.
Peel and core the pineapple, then cut into slices about 1 cm thick. Chop the remaining shallot and garlic and slice the scallions.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pot and saute the remaining shallot, garlic and ginger until fragrant. Add the pineapple and turn gently for 1–2 minutes.
Arrange the pineapple on the bottom of the pot and set the fish on top. Add the marinade, caramel sauce and enough water to come nearly level with the fish.
Bring to a simmer, skim if needed, then reduce the heat to low. Braise for 35–40 minutes without stirring; gently tilt the pot occasionally to baste the fish.
When the sauce is glossy and the fish is cooked through, adjust the seasoning and finish with scallions and pepper.

ca-thu-kho-tieu.name: Pepper-Braised King Mackerel
aliases: Vietnamese King Mackerel Braised with Pepper
King Mackerel Braised in Pepper Sauce
ca-thu-kho-tieu.serving_basis: Four portions of braised fish served with rice.
ca-thu-kho-tieu.description: King mackerel is lightly seared, then simmered in fish sauce, pepper and a little sugar. The savory, gently peppery glaze pairs well with a simple vegetable soup.
ca-thu-kho-tieu.finished_dish: Firm, moist fish steaks coated with a lightly thickened pepper sauce.
ca-thu-kho-tieu.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and cucumber or boiled vegetables.
tips: Pat the fish dry before searing so it browns evenly and splatters less.
Use a wide spatula when turning the fish to keep each steak intact.
Add some pepper near the end for a clearer aroma without bitterness.
ca-thu-kho-tieu.image_alt: A blue-and-white bowl of pepper-braised king mackerel steaks with green peppercorns and glossy sauce.
ca-thu-kho-tieu.time_note: About 55 minutes, including 10 minutes to marinate the fish.

preparation_steps: Rinse the fish briefly and pat dry. Marinate with a little fish sauce, pepper and shallot for 10 minutes.
Mix the remaining fish sauce with water, sugar, salt, seasoning powder and chili sauce. Chop the garlic and slice the scallions; dust the fish lightly with cornstarch.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sear the fish over medium heat until lightly browned on both sides. Transfer to a plate.
Saute the garlic in the remaining oil. Pour in the braising mixture and bring to a gentle boil, then return the fish to the pan.
Cover loosely and simmer over low heat for 12–15 minutes. Turn the fish once carefully so both sides absorb the sauce.
When the sauce lightly coats the fish, adjust the seasoning and finish with pepper and scallions.

ca-chim-kho-rieng.name: Pomfret Braised with Galangal
aliases: Vietnamese Pomfret Braised with Galangal and Lemongrass
ca-chim-kho-rieng.serving_basis: Four portions of braised fish for a family meal.
ca-chim-kho-rieng.description: Pomfret is braised over galangal and lemongrass, with a little turmeric for a warm golden-brown color. Ginger and pepper perfume the sauce, which pairs well with rice and vegetables.
ca-chim-kho-rieng.finished_dish: Firm, well-seasoned fish with fragrant galangal and lemongrass, coated in a reduced glossy sauce.
ca-chim-kho-rieng.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and boiled vegetables, including a few softened pieces of galangal.
tips: Rub the fish with salt and ginger, then pat dry before marinating.
Layer galangal and lemongrass under the fish to protect it from sticking and perfume the braise.
Avoid stirring; tilt the pot to baste the fish with the sauce.

ca-chim-kho-rieng.time_note: About 105 minutes, including 25 minutes to marinate the fish.

preparation_steps: Rub the fish with salt, rinse and pat dry. Marinate with ginger, shallot, garlic, fish sauce, salt, seasoning powder, pepper and turmeric for 25 minutes.
Slice half the galangal and bruise the rest. Bruise and cut the lemongrass, slice the scallions and prepare the caramel sauce.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and briefly sear both sides of the fish until firm, then set aside.
Layer sliced galangal and lemongrass in a pot. Add the fish, crushed galangal, marinade, caramel sauce and oyster sauce.
Bring to a gentle boil, baste the fish with the liquid, then add enough stock to nearly cover it. Reduce the heat and braise for 40–45 minutes until tender and the sauce is reduced.
Taste and adjust the seasoning, finish with pepper and scallions, then let the fish rest in the pot for a few minutes before serving.
